title: Stacked headers written before 0.3.0 read with the bottom line's labels only
body:
Before 0.3.0 the writer did not pad a ragged column's header words. On an upper line of a stacked header, where that column's word is empty, every word after it sits left of its column. Under a dashed rule the 0.3.0 reader (Head::find, src/read.rs:209-216) requires every header word to start on a rule run, so it takes those lines for preamble. The cells read correctly; the labels come back as the bottom line's words alone.

nail-benchmarks writes runs.tbl in this shape (cloud-search/src/scores/runs.rs:277-294: a ragged query column first, then stacked run names). Its Frame reader rejects a file with no '#= format' line, but a file written by toil 0.2.x has that line and unpadded headers. Nobody has checked whether such files exist on disk. Options: rewrite them with 0.3.0, read them by position, or let the reader accept a word left of its column on an upper line.
